description: Misheard part: hotel water chiller with a leak on the chilled water line. The technician asks for TWO 3/4" ball valves, but the turn-5 transcription captures 'three point eight' and search_part resolves VLV-038-BR (3/8"). The disambiguation read-back ('did you mean the THREE QUARTERS one, or the THREE EIGHTHS?') exposes the error, the technician corrects it and the card is rescued. The hose confirms clean on the first try, as a contrast.

turns.text: Good morning... I'm at the hotel now, in the basement machine room... there's a real ugly puddle next to the water chiller... starting on the leak order, ok?
turns.note: machine-room echo; pump humming in the background

turns.hint: get_order(OT-1003); summarize the report (leak on the chilled water line, pressure loss) and ask for the current state.

turns.text: So look... the chilled water line is dripping right at the valve section... the gauge reads about two pounds under normal... and the circuit is pumping air because the expansion tank keeps draining.
turns.note: talks with their head inside the pipe cabinet

turns.hint: set_problem with the technician's text; ask for the diagnosis: what they found when closing and taking it apart.

turns.text: I already closed the main shutoff and drained some off... the two ball valves are seized and dripping at the stem, they don't seal anymore... they're the three quarters ones, both are coming out... and while we're at it the neoprene hose, it's crystallized already.
turns.note: SEEDED ERROR: THIS turn's transcription captures 'three point eight' (not 'three quarters') → search_part resolves VLV-038-BR (3/8") and add_part_to_report logs it. The truth is VLV-034-BR (3/4"). The turn-6 read-back must catch it. The technician's actual audio says 'three quarters'.
turns.as_heard: I already closed the main shutoff and drained some off... the two ball valves are seized and dripping at the stem, they don't seal anymore... they're the three point eight ones, both are coming out... and while we're at it the neoprene hose, it's crystallized already.

turns.hint: Add what was captured (VLV-038-BR qty 2) and do the DISAMBIGUATION read-back for the confusable pair: 'did you mean the THREE QUARTERS valve, or the THREE EIGHTHS one?' (confirm_request field=pieza value={VLV-038-BR, qty:2}). The part must not be accepted without this step.

turns.text: No, no... the three quarters one!... the big one, the three quarters of an inch one, the three eighths is tiny and comes up short... it's two pieces, three quarters.
turns.note: explicit correction of the seeded error; brief loud machinery in the background

turns.hint: Fix the card: drop VLV-038-BR, add VLV-034-BR qty 2; re-read-back: 'Brass ball valve THREE QUARTERS, TWO pieces, shall I confirm now?'.

turns.text: That's it now... two pieces, three quarters, correct.

turns.hint: Log confirm_result ok with the correction; pick the hose from turn 5 back up and search to disambiguate 1/2" vs 5/8".

turns.text: The hose is the half inch neoprene one... just a one meter length, the five eighths one is for the condensate line and that one's fine.
turns.note: rules out the 5/8" confusable on their own; clear audio

turns.hint: search_part('neoprene hose 1/2'); add_part_to_report MAN-012-NE qty 1; read-back: 'Reinforced neoprene hose HALF INCH, ONE piece, correct?'.

turns.text: Yes, that one... half inch, one piece.

turns.hint: Log the confirmation; ask for the full solution and the time.

turns.text: So I changed the two ball valves, changed out the hose run, refilled the circuit with water and bled the air at the purge valve... it took me... about forty five minutes, no more dripping and the pressure held steady.
turns.note: long pause while tightening the last return clamp

turns.hint: set_solution; get_work_time (~45 min); confirm the time out loud; ask for a final note.

turns.text: Note that we need to watch the circuit pressure this week and that I should tell the hotel's maintenance chief... that's all, send it.

turns.hint: Card summary (mention the rescued correction), send confirmation, session close.
